answer: A stake-bonded reputation graph resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and peers vouch for one another only after verified work. A fake identity is an island - no vouching history, no trade partners - so it cannot borrow trust. If one is caught, slashing cuts a canyon through its linked accounts, wiping the whole cluster stake at once. Honest behavior sends a ripple of attestations outward, raising the cost of forging many believable histories far above any single scam payoff.
